chapter: Minton's, bop and the Monk circle
title: Monk at Minton's in the 1930s
summary: She saw Monk in New York in the 1930s and grew close at Minton's, where bop musicians jammed because 52nd Street had no work for them.

story.theme_name: Charlie Parker, Dizzy and the bebop revolution
story.community_name: Playing with and understanding Thelonious Monk

blocks.x: I'd like to go back to Thelonious Monk. You first saw him in Kansas City? When was the next time you saw him?
I saw him in New York during the 30's. We became very, very good friends. In fact, Bud Powell, Monk, and I were inseparable. During the 40's that was every day, every night, all the time.
During the 30's what did you do?

Really I got close with him when he was working at Minton's. That was before anybody ever heard of bop. I was living at the Dewey Square Hotel, 118th and Seventh Avenue and I used to go around to Minton's every night to the jam sessions and Monk was playing there.
How did Monk happen to be at Minton's?
All the bop musicians were jamming or playing there every night because there was no work for them on 52nd Street. Nobody understood what they were playing.
